subject: Stability review & action summary — May 24 reduced throughput
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Gwen Park <gwen@alkira.io>, Roy Singh <roy.s@alkira.io>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Stability review & action summary — May 24 reduced throughput

Hi Gwen / Roy —

Thanks again for your patience while we investigated the reduced throughput you saw on May 24. Attached is a short timeline we compiled and a summary of immediate mitigations we implemented. I want to be transparent about what happened, what we've already done to stabilize your traffic, and the concrete actions we're committing to.

Summary (short):
- Impact window: May 24, 2027 14:12–15:06 UTC — elevated tail latency and intermittent request errors for a subset of inference routes.
- Root cause (investigation in progress): allocator behavior + autoscaler interaction that triggered memory fragmentation on a small set of quantized-p8 model instances.
- Customer effect: transient 500/timeout errors for ~6% of requests during peak tail; average latency recovered after automated fallback.

What we already did:
- Rolled a temporary routing policy to fallback to a compatible model variant (reduced quantization aggressiveness) for affected routes — this removed errors within ~9 minutes.
- Disabled the autoscaler heuristic that exercised aggressive instance preemption in the 14:00–15:00 UTC window.
- Collected heap/dmesg/kernel traces and preserved the affected instances for deeper forensic analysis.

Next steps we will take (more details in attached timeline):
- Engineering: perform a targeted patch to the autoscaler to avoid preempting warmed GPU instances when KV cache is active (owner: Hannah). ETA: 2 weeks.
- Runtime: add a quantization-safety check during kernel selection to avoid mixing kernels that increase fragmentation risk (owner: Runtime team, Marcus). ETA: 3 weeks.
- Post-incident: longer-term scheduler hardening and a canary rollout for the patch with customer-facing traffic simulation. ETA: 6 weeks.

Can we schedule a 30-minute debrief next week to walk through the timeline and the action plan? We can also share the full traces under an NDA if helpful.

Attachments: 20270528-stability-timeline.csv (short event log)

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

Subject: Technical timeline & preliminary root cause notes

Hi Gwen / Irene / Marcus —

Following up with more technical context and the minute-level timeline we pulled for the affected fleet. I've pasted the condensed timeline below and attached the full CSV to the shared Drive folder.

Condensed timeline (UTC):
- 14:10:02: autoscaler triggered an aggressive scale-in event for a subset of p4d-like pools due to a transient perceived drop in CPU utilization.
- 14:11:40: first user-facing increase in tail latency observed on model route /models/rosetta-11q-p8.
- 14:12:07–14:21: occasional OOM-retry loops on 3 instances that had recently received a quantized kernel selection. Kernel selection logs show mixed kernel sets that increase device-side fragmentation.
- 14:21:00: Automated fallback routing engaged to rosetta-11q-p8-stable variant — error volume dropped ~92% over next 9 minutes.
- 15:06:00: all measurable error rates back to baseline; monitoring shows residual increased memory pressure for a small subset of instances.

Preliminary root cause (summary):
- The sequence appears to be: autoscaler preempted warmed instances -> warmed KV caches became cold on new instances -> kernel selector chose an aggressive quantized kernel combination on warmup -> the combination led to fragmentation and intermittent OOMs under peak tail workloads.

Mitigations committed (short-term):
- Disable aggressive preemption path in autoscaler for pools with KV-active instances (immediate, done).
- Enforce kernel-selection safety checks to prefer kernel sets with lower fragmentation signature for quantized models (in-progress).
- Add minute-level per-route error exports for customers (Irene will share per-route CSV).

We will produce a final RCA with code references and playbook changes once we've completed the forensic trace analysis.

Happy to jump on the call Tuesday — can take technical questions and walk the traces.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Engineer, Runtime Reliability
hannah@redwood.com

Longer-term (planning):
